Possible, but aggressive
🟠
So I would make one more v4 revision, but it does not require redesigning the project.
🔴 1. Biggest issue: SAR single-image VQA is not actually guaranteed
This is the most important gap I found.
Your spec says:
single_image_vqa → geochat
But the PS explicitly includes a single SAR image in the supported input scope. ([GitHub](https://github.com/aditya-kr86/sih2026/blob/main/ps_2026/SIH26167.md?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
GeoChat is a remote-sensing VLM, but its published architecture and training ecosystem are not equivalent to a dedicated SAR VLM. Its paper describes image-level VQA, captioning, scene classification and grounding, while its training is built around LLaVA-1.5/Vicuna and remote-sensing instruction data. ([Open Access CVF](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/papers/Kuckreja_GeoChat_Grounded_Large_Vision-Language_Model_for_Remote_Sensing_CVPR_2024_paper.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
Meanwhile, EarthGPT explicitly targets multisensor RS interpretation and reports optical, SAR and infrared data in its MMRS-1M dataset. ([IEEE Xplore](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10547418?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
Why this matters
Your current architecture could end up doing:
SAR GeoTIFF ↓ GeoChat ↓ "answer"
without demonstrating that the model actually understands SAR.
That is dangerous for an ISRO/SAC evaluation.
Fix
Add a sensor-aware VQA router:
single_image_vqa │ ├── optical/multispectral │ ↓ │ geochat │ └── SAR ↓ sar_vqa_capability │ ┌───────┴────────┐ │ │ SAR-adapted VLM deterministic / Earth observation SAR feature model tools
And explicitly define:
A generic RGB-oriented RS-VLM must not be declared a valid SAR-VQA implementation merely because a SAR image can technically be converted into an RGB PNG.
That is a very important scientific distinction.
🔴 2. BigEarthNet.txt does not automatically solve SAR VQA
Your adaptation strategy is good, but there's a hidden issue.
BigEarthNet.txt is genuinely highly relevant: it contains 464,044 co-registered Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 pairs and ~9.6M textual annotations, including VQA and referring-expression tasks. ([RSIAG TU Berlin](https://txt.bigearth.net/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
That's excellent for your project.
But:
BigEarthNet.txt ↓ LoRA ↓ GeoChat
is not automatically valid.
You need to decide exactly how the multispectral/SAR tensors enter the model.
For example:
Sentinel-1 SAR ↓ 1/2 channel raster ↓ ? ↓ GeoChat vision encoder
GeoChat's published configuration uses a CLIP ViT-L/14 336px vision tower, so simply supplying arbitrary SAR channels is not equivalent to its original input distribution. ([GitHub](https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/GeoChat?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
Add a sensor adapter
I recommend:
Sensor Adapter │ ┌────────────┼─────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ RGB MSI/S2 SAR │ │ │ │ band selection/ │ │ normalization │ │ │ └──────────► model input ◄────┘
But the SAR branch needs an explicit representation strategy.
For example:
SAR VV SAR VH VV/VH log-scaled backscatter optional texture ↓ SAR → 3-channel representation ↓ VLM
Do not pretend this makes the model inherently SAR-native.
Document it as:
"SAR input adapter for VLM inference"
and evaluate it separately.
🔴 3. Your temporal engine detects "change", but not necessarily "what changed"
This is the second major technical risk.
Your deterministic pipeline is:
T1 T2 ↓ difference ↓ threshold ↓ mask ↓ area
That's excellent for change detection.
But consider:
"What changed?"
A binary difference mask can tell you:
Something changed here.
It cannot necessarily tell you:
A building was constructed here.
or:
Vegetation was removed.
or:
A water body expanded.
Those are semantic change interpretations.
You need to distinguish two levels
Add:
LEVEL 1 — Physical / image change pixel/spectral/backscatter difference LEVEL 2 — Semantic change building road vegetation water bare soil etc.
Your response must know which level it achieved.
For example:
Detected change: 3 regions
Change type: spectral/spatial change
Semantic class: not determined
is scientifically honest.
Whereas:
"A new building appeared"
should only be generated if a semantic classifier/detector actually supports that claim.
Add this rule
A change mask does not constitute semantic change classification. The system must distinguish change_detected from change_type_inferred. No semantic class may be asserted solely from pixel difference.
This is a very important addition.
🔴 4. Optical-SAR fusion is still too conceptual
Your current specification says:
optical evidence + SAR evidence ↓ spatial fusion ↓ fused result
Architecturally excellent.
But an evaluator can ask:
"What exactly is your fusion algorithm?"
Right now the answer isn't sufficiently concrete.
You need one actual baseline.
For example, for a water query:
Optical branch
available bands ↓ NDWI / MNDWI if valid ↓ water candidate mask
SAR branch
VV/VH or available polarization ↓ calibrated/normalized backscatter ↓ development-validated water candidate
Fusion
Optical water evidence + SAR water evidence ↓ spatial alignment ↓ agreement / weighted evidence ↓ fused water mask
But the weights/thresholds must be derived from development data.
Your specification already correctly prohibits universal SAR thresholds.
I would add:
Every mandatory optical-SAR demonstration must use an explicitly implemented task-specific fusion rule or model. "Fusion" cannot mean merely displaying two independent results side by side. The contribution of each modality must be identifiable in the evidence object and ablation/test output.
That directly strengthens Demo 4.
🟠 5. Co-registration needs a quality gate, not merely a checker
Currently:
CompatibilityChecker CoRegistrationChecker
is good.
But registration can fail.
Suppose T1 and T2 are shifted by 4 pixels.
Your system might produce:
BUILDING CHANGE
when the reality is:
registration error
Add:
Registration ↓ alignment residual ↓ quality score ↓ PASS / WARN / REJECT
For example:
{ "registration_status": "PASS", "method": "...", "residual_px": 0.73, "overlap_fraction": 0.94 }
Do not hardcode 0.73 or a universal threshold.
The threshold should be configuration/development validated.
And:
If registration quality is insufficient, temporal analysis must stop or be explicitly marked unreliable.
This is especially important for the hidden Cartosat/RISAT evaluation.
🟠 6. Temporal change has a major false-change problem
Your change engine should explicitly consider:
illumination differences
seasonal differences
crop cycles
atmospheric effects
sensor/viewing geometry
SAR speckle
incidence angle
preprocessing differences
resolution differences
shadows
clouds for optical data
Otherwise:
T1 = summer T2 = winter
could produce massive "change".
Your current verification layer mentions temporal consistency, but I would add a dedicated:
TemporalChangeQualityGate
acquisition dates season sensor resolution CRS grid illumination metadata where available cloud/nodata SAR acquisition geometry where available registration quality ↓ CHANGE QUALITY
The system can then say:
"Change detected, but seasonal/domain differences may contribute to the observed difference."
That is much more defensible.
🟠 7. ChangeChat license handling is correct — but your broader license audit needs strengthening
Your new ChangeChat gate is excellent.
But the same principle needs to apply to all datasets and dependencies.
GeoChat's model card currently lists Apache-2.0 for the GeoChat-7B checkpoint. ([Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/MBZUAI/geochat-7B/blob/main/README.md?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
However, GeoChat itself is built on LLaVA-1.5/Vicuna-derived components. The GeoChat repository explicitly says its model is fine-tuned over LLaVA-1.5 and uses Vicuna-generated instruction data. ([GitHub](https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/GeoChat?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
Therefore your audit should be:
SatQuery │ ├── GeoChat code license ├── GeoChat checkpoint license ├── base model license ├── vision encoder license ├── tokenizer/model components ├── dataset licenses └── third-party package licenses
Don't simply record:
GeoChat = Apache-2.0
and conclude the entire dependency chain is cleared.
Add:
License status is dependency-chain based. A top-level repository license does not automatically clear inherited model weights, datasets, base models, or bundled assets.
🟠 8. Your benchmark licensing section needs attention
This is easy to miss.
For example, VRSBench's text annotations are CC-BY-4.0, but its repository states that some images originate from DOTA and are restricted to academic use. ([GitHub](https://github.com/lx709/VRSBench?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
Another dataset card describes VRSBench as non-commercial. ([Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/xiang709/VRSBench/blob/main/README.md?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
Therefore:
Don't copy benchmark imagery into your public GitHub repository just because the benchmark itself is public.
Your architecture should have:
data/ benchmark/ README.md DOWNLOAD_INSTRUCTIONS.md
rather than committing copyrighted/restricted benchmark images.
This should be part of the license audit.
🟠 9. BigEarthNet.txt is excellent, but make v2.0 your backup
Your decision to use BigEarthNet.txt is sensible.
The official BigEarthNet.txt site describes 464,044 co-registered S1/S2 pairs and ~9.6M text annotations. ([RSIAG TU Berlin](https://txt.bigearth.net/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
But it is a 2026 dataset, and your own engineering window is short.
BigEarthNet v2.0 is a much more established backup containing 549,488 paired Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 patches, with the official site stating its dataset license is CDLA-Permissive 1.0. ([BigEarthNet](https://bigearth.net/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
So add:
Primary adaptation source: BigEarthNet.txt Backup RS adaptation source: BigEarthNet v2.0 / other verified open RS dataset
But don't silently substitute the dataset and still claim:
"fine-tuned using BigEarthNet.txt."
The report must state which dataset was actually used.
🟠 10. Your "P0 grounding" needs clarification
You currently say:
P0: grounding pathway
But if GeoChat fails, what exactly performs grounding?
If your fallback is:
generic CV detector
that's not necessarily equivalent to:
text-guided region grounding
You need a deterministic fallback such as:
query ↓ object/category extraction ↓ available detector/segmentation capability ↓ candidate regions ↓ text-region matching ↓ bbox
or make the fallback explicitly:
GROUNDING UNAVAILABLE
rather than falsely calling another detector "text-guided grounding."
This follows your Golden Rule.
🟠 11. Your confidence design is good, but define confidence types
You currently have:
confidence: 0.84
and correctly state that it shouldn't be called calibrated probability.
I'd go one step further.
Use:
model_confidence evidence_confidence measurement_quality registration_quality fusion_agreement
rather than:
overall_confidence = 0.84
unless you actually calibrate it.
This is consistent with the project's existing direction of separating geometric, temporal, physical, provenance and statistical verification rather than inventing one unsupported reliability score. ([GitHub](https://github.com/bishuk-dev/SIH-26167-SATQuery?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
🟠 12. Your P0/P1 classification has one contradiction
You say:
P0 — single-image VQA pathway
P1 — GeoChat live inference
But how can single-image VQA actually be P0 if GeoChat is P1?
You have:
P0: single-image VQA pathway P1: GeoChat live inference
These are potentially contradictory.
Fix
Separate:
P0: VQA workflow + valid RS-adapted implementation/fallback contract P1: specific large-model live inference
Then:
VQA capability = P0 GeoChat implementation = P1
But if the SIH requirement demands a real adapted VLM, your final build must still have at least one valid adapted RS-VL component. A generic fallback alone cannot satisfy that requirement.
🔴 13. The hardest requirement remains RS adaptation
This is the biggest project-level risk after SAR.
The SIH description explicitly says:
A generic LLM or VLM without remote-sensing adaptation will not satisfy the requirements. ([GitHub](https://github.com/aditya-kr86/sih2026/blob/main/ps_2026/SIH26167.md?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
Your plan technically addresses this with:
BigEarthNet.txt ↓ LoRA
but your acceptance test only says:
"Can demonstrate BigEarthNet.txt adaptation"
That isn't strong enough.
You need to distinguish:
ADAPTATION PIPELINE EXISTS
from:
ADAPTATION ACTUALLY COMPLETED
and:
ADAPTED MODEL EVALUATED
Add three states
RS_ADAPTATION_PIPELINE_READY RS_ADAPTATION_TRAINED RS_ADAPTATION_EVALUATED
Only the latter two should be presented as model adaptation results.
🟠 14. Your 8-day schedule remains the biggest operational risk
I would not change the architecture because of this.
But the workload is substantial:
GIS ingestion + FastAPI + React + agent controller + GeoChat + LoRA + change detection + registration + SAR processing + optical-SAR fusion + evidence + verification + reports + benchmarks + testing
That's too much for one developer in eight days.
It becomes much more realistic with parallel team ownership:
Person A → backend/controller/GIS Person B → ML/VLM/LoRA Person C → temporal + SAR Person D → frontend/reports/evaluation
If you are working alone, P2 should effectively disappear until the final day.
🟠 15. Windows should not be the primary development environment
Your specification currently says four environments:
env-core env-geochat env-changechat env-croma
On Windows, PyTorch + CUDA + GDAL + Rasterio + research repositories + Flash Attention can become an unnecessary battle.
I strongly recommend:
Windows host ↓ WSL2 Ubuntu ↓ NVIDIA CUDA ↓ Docker / Conda / venv
The GUI can still run in the browser on Windows.
Don't make WSL2 mandatory if your actual environment proves stable natively, but make it the recommended reproducible environment.
🟠 16. You need a "demo truthfulness" layer
This is something I strongly recommend adding.
Your final UI should distinguish:
MODEL RESULT DETERMINISTIC RESULT HEURISTIC RESULT FALLBACK RESULT DEMO RESULT
For example:
Analysis source: ● Deterministic Change Engine Semantic interpretation: ● Not available Measurement: ● Computed from raster geometry Explanation: ● Rule-based
This makes the project much more credible.
🟠 17. Don't let the UI imply more than the backend actually did
For example:
Confidence: 91%
looks like a calibrated probability.
Instead:
Evidence confidence HIGH Basis: • optical evidence: strong • SAR evidence: moderate • spatial agreement: high • registration: PASS
or, if you have a validated score:
Calibrated confidence: 0.91 Calibration method: ... Validation set: ...
Your existing scientific-integrity rules are already moving in this direction.
🟢 18. Your agent architecture is actually one of the strongest parts
I would not replace your deterministic router with a fully autonomous LLM agent.
Your:
query ↓ query contract ↓ capability registry ↓ available models ↓ permitted workflow ↓ execution
is much easier to audit.
This also matches how other current SatQuery implementations are approaching the problem: constrained workflow selection rather than letting an LLM freely invent tools. ([GitHub](https://github.com/bishuk-dev/SIH-26167-SATQuery?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
Keep this.
🟢 19. The Evidence Store is an excellent design decision
This:
{ "claim": "...", "source": "...", "evidence_type": "...", "bbox": [...], "model": "...", "inputs": [...] }
is exactly the kind of structure that makes your project more than:
"ChatGPT for satellite images."
I would keep it central.
🟢 20. Your numerical guard is absolutely worth keeping
This:
raster → measurement engine → number → response generator
rather than:
image → LLM → "approximately 18.4 km²"
is one of the clearest engineering differentiators.
Keep it exactly as a core principle.
One more important issue: your public GitHub should NOT contain everything
Your final repository should not contain:
models/ huge checkpoints data/ benchmark imagery data/ restricted datasets
Instead:
models/ README.md download instructions checksums
and:
data/ README.md manifests/ sample_metadata/
Use scripts to acquire permitted assets.
This also makes the final SIH submission much cleaner.
The changes I would actually make to v3
I would not rewrite the entire document.
Add these 8 sections/rules:
Add 8.6 — Sensor-specific VQA
Single-image VQA must be sensor-aware. Optical/multispectral VQA: approved RS-VLM pathway. SAR VQA: dedicated SAR-capable/adapted pathway. A SAR raster converted to RGB for convenience must not automatically be treated as evidence that the model is SAR-aware. The capability registry must expose sensor compatibility explicitly.
Add 16.1 — Semantic-change boundary
Binary/image change ≠ semantic change. The system must distinguish: change_detected change_region change_measurement change_type_inferred A semantic class must not be asserted solely from a binary difference mask.
Add 16.2 — Registration quality gate
Registration must produce: registration_status method residual/error metric overlap transformed grid metadata Insufficient registration quality must cause rejection or an explicit uncertainty state.
Add 16.3 — Temporal confound warning
Check for: season acquisition geometry illumination clouds/nodata SAR speckle/geometry sensor differences resolution differences Potential confounders must appear in the final evidence/report.
Add 17.1 — Actual optical-SAR fusion algorithm
Require one executable, documented task-specific fusion baseline.
Add 15.1 — Adaptation status
RS_ADAPTATION_PIPELINE_READY RS_ADAPTATION_TRAINED RS_ADAPTATION_EVALUATED
Add 4.2 — Complete dependency license audit
code weights base models datasets benchmark imagery third-party assets
Add 44 — Public repository hygiene
Never commit: restricted benchmark imagery unlicensed model weights large checkpoints private evaluation data secrets/API keys Commit: manifests hashes download scripts licenses preprocessing metadata reproducibility instructions
The final risk hierarchy
After these changes, I would think about the project like this:
🔴 Must actively solve
SAR single-image VQA
Actual RS-adapted VLM implementation
Semantic vs pixel-level change distinction
Concrete optical-SAR fusion algorithm
Registration quality
Temporal false-change handling
🟠 Must manage
GeoChat compute
BigEarthNet adaptation time
Dataset/model licensing
Benchmark reproduction
Windows/GDAL/PyTorch environment
Eight-day workload
Public repository data restrictions
🟢 Already very well handled
Agent routing
graceful degradation
ChangeChat failure
numerical hallucination
evidence provenance
execution trace
daily Git checkpoints
report generation
scientific integrity
P0/P1/P2 prioritization
One especially important conclusion
I would not add more models to solve these risks.
The temptation now would be:
GeoChat EarthGPT ChangeChat CROMA Grounding DINO SAM CLIP another SAR model another change model ...
That would make the project worse.
Your current architecture's strongest idea is:
specialist models are replaceable components; the evidence-driven SatQuery workflow is the product.
GeoChat already supports image-level VQA, captioning and grounding, while EarthGPT demonstrates that multisensor optical/SAR VLMs are technically possible. BigEarthNet.txt now gives you a particularly relevant S1/S2 image-text resource. ([Open Access CVF](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/papers/Kuckreja_GeoChat_Grounded_Large_Vision-Language_Model_for_Remote_Sensing_CVPR_2024_paper.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# SATQUERY AI — FINAL AUTHORITATIVE BUILD SPECIFICATION (v4 MASTER PLAN)

**Problem Statement ID:** 26167  
**Sponsor:** ISRO / Department of Space / Space Applications Centre (SAC)  
**Revision:** v4 — Final Locked Master Plan  
**Supersedes:** All earlier drafts including v3  
**Date:** 2026-09-21  

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is the frozen specification. Read Section 0 and Section 42
> (Antigravity Execution Protocol) before doing anything else.
> Architecture changes after this revision require explicit human approval.

---

# 0. NON-NEGOTIABLE ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES

Build SatQuery AI as an evidence-driven, agentic remote-sensing
analysis system.

It must NOT be implemented as:

    User → generic LLM → answer

It must instead operate as:

    UNDERSTAND → CHECK → CHOOSE → ANALYZE → VERIFY → EXPLAIN

The system must understand the user's query, inspect the supplied
remote-sensing data, determine which specialist capability is
required, execute the appropriate tools/models, verify the result
against computational evidence, and present the answer with visual
evidence, confidence, and execution provenance.

No specialist model is allowed to become a single point of failure.

Every mandatory PS capability must have an executable baseline
implementation independent of optional large-model inference. Large
RS-VLMs improve the system when available. They must NEVER determine
whether the core SatQuery application can start, accept data,
validate data, route tasks, perform deterministic analysis, produce
evidence, show execution traces, or generate reports.

**THE GOLDEN RULE:**

> The planned architecture is not evidence that a capability
> exists. A capability becomes "implemented" only after its code
> executes successfully on the current machine and passes its
> acceptance test.

Never report a feature as complete merely because its code exists.

---

# 1. PS REQUIREMENTS — MUST ALL BE IMPLEMENTED

1. Remote-sensing image upload.
2. Input compatibility checking.
3. Optical/multispectral imagery.
4. SAR imagery.
5. Co-registered optical + SAR pairs.
6. Bi-temporal imagery.
7. Single-image VQA — **sensor-aware** (optical AND SAR).
8. At least one additional single-image task: grounding OR
   captioning/scene description.
9. Bi-temporal change understanding — **with semantic-change
   boundary** (distinguishing pixel change from semantic change).
10. Optical-SAR paired analysis — **with a concrete, implemented
    fusion algorithm**.
11. At least one remote-sensing-adapted VLM/VL component.
12. Fine-tuning/adaptation using BigEarthNet.txt or another
    appropriate open-source remote-sensing training dataset.
13. Agentic orchestration: query interpretation, task selection,
    tool/model selection, sequencing, execution, integration.
14. Visual evidence.
15. Confidence — **decomposed by type** (see §25.1).
16. Execution summary / observable execution trace.
17. Downloadable reports.
18. Public benchmark evaluation.
19. Clean separation of training/validation/public test/hidden test.
20. Graceful failure for unsupported or incompatible inputs.

The final implementation must directly map every one of these
requirements to a working module.

---

# 2. FINAL ARCHITECTURE

```
                         SATQUERY AI
                              │
                              ▼
                    ┌──────────────────┐
                    │ Upload / Gateway │
                    └────────┬─────────┘
                             │
                             ▼
                  ┌─────────────────────┐
                  │ Data Readiness Gate │
                  └──────────┬──────────┘
                             │
                             ▼
                  ┌─────────────────────┐
                  │   Query Contract    │
                  └──────────┬──────────┘
                             │
                             ▼
                  ┌─────────────────────┐
                  │ Capability Router   │
                  │ (sensor-aware)      │
                  └──────────┬──────────┘
                             │
          ┌──────────────────┼───────────────────┐
          │                  │                   │
          ▼                  ▼                   ▼
    single_image_vqa   change_engine       optical_sar_fusion
          │                  │                   │
     ┌────┴────┐      ┌─────┴─────┐        ┌────┴────┐
     │         │      │           │        │         │
   optical   SAR    physical   semantic  optical   SAR
   VQA       VQA    change     change    branch    branch
                     (L1)      (L2)        │         │
          │                  │             └────┬────┘
          │                  │                  │
          └──────────────────┼──────────────────┘
                             │
                             ▼
                      Evidence Store
                             │
                             ▼
                   Verification Layer
                             │
                             ▼
                 Demo Truthfulness Layer
                             │
                             ▼
                    Response Generator
                             │
                             ▼
                         GUI / Map
                             │
                             ▼
                     Reports / Exports
```

Optional enhancement (never a dependency):

    Optical + SAR → croma → task-specific head → additional evidence

CROMA must remain optional at all times.

---

# 3. FEASIBILITY GATE (RUN BEFORE ANY MODEL WORK)

Do not assume GPU availability.

Create:

    scripts/system_check.py

It must detect: OS, Python version, PyTorch version, CUDA version,
CUDA availability, GPU count, GPU name, total VRAM, free VRAM, CPU,
RAM, disk space, Git, Git LFS, Docker if available.

Output a readable report and classify the machine:

    PROFILE A — FULL GPU        (≥48GB VRAM class — A100/L20/A6000)
    PROFILE B — LIMITED GPU     (roughly 12–24GB — consumer GPUs)
    PROFILE C — CPU ONLY

Do NOT use a guessed fixed VRAM number as the sole decision
mechanism — empirically test model loading and inference via the
preflight scripts in Section 4.

---

# 4. MODEL PREFLIGHT (INCLUDING LICENSE GATES)

Create:

    scripts/test_geochat.py
    scripts/test_changechat.py
    scripts/test_croma.py

Each script is isolated. Each test must: load environment, load
checkpoint, load processor/tokenizer, load one small test
image/pair, execute one inference, parse output, and return
PASS/FAIL with a reason.

Example:

    GEOCHAT PREFLIGHT
    -----------------
    checkpoint: PASS
    processor: PASS
    image load: PASS
    inference: PASS
    output parse: PASS

    STATUS: READY

If a model fails: STATUS: UNAVAILABLE. Do not allow a failed model
to break the application.

## 4.1 CHANGECHAT LICENSE GATE

Runs BEFORE any ChangeChat integration work, and before the 3-hour
integration budget (§8.2) starts counting.

1. Verify the repository's current LICENSE file and any separate
   license terms attached to the pretrained checkpoint/weights.
   A permissive code license does NOT automatically mean the
   downloaded weights carry the same terms — check both independently.
2. Confirm that redistribution/use in an SIH competition submission
   is permitted.
3. Record repository URL, code license, weight license terms, and
   verification date in `docs/model_licenses.md`.
4. If licensing is unclear, incompatible, or cannot be verified with
   confidence, mark ChangeChat `BLOCKED_LICENSE` and stop — do not
   proceed to inference preflight.
5. The deterministic temporal change pipeline (§16) remains the
   official implementation regardless of the outcome of this gate.

Do the same license verification for GeoChat and CROMA before
relying on their weights, and record all three in
`docs/model_licenses.md`.

## 4.2 COMPLETE DEPENDENCY-CHAIN LICENSE AUDIT *(v4 addition)*

> [!CAUTION]
> A top-level repository license does NOT automatically clear
> inherited model weights, datasets, base models, or bundled assets.
> License status is dependency-chain based.

For every model and dataset used, audit and record in
`docs/model_licenses.md`:

```
SatQuery AI
│
├── GeoChat
│   ├── GeoChat code license (Apache-2.0)
│   ├── GeoChat checkpoint license
│   ├── Base model: LLaVA-1.5 → Vicuna-v1.5 → Llama 2 (Meta Community License)
│   ├── Vision encoder: CLIP ViT-L/14 (MIT / OpenAI)
│   ├── Tokenizer / model components
│   ├── Training dataset licenses (GPT-4 generated instruction data — verify ToS)
│   └── Third-party package licenses
│
├── ChangeChat
│   ├── Repository license (NONE — default copyright applies)
│   ├── Checkpoint license
│   └── Base model chain (CLIP + Vicuna)
│
├── CROMA
│   ├── Repository license
│   ├── Checkpoint license
│   └── Training data license
│
├── Datasets
│   ├── BigEarthNet.txt — license terms
│   ├── BigEarthNet v2.0 — CDLA-Permissive 1.0
│   ├── VRSBench — CC-BY-4.0 annotations, BUT some images from DOTA (academic-only)
│   ├── RSVQA — license terms
│   └── CDVQA — license terms
│
└── Benchmark imagery
    └── DO NOT commit restricted benchmark images to public repository
```

Each entry must record: source URL, code license, weight/data license,
verification date, SIH-competition compatibility assessment.

---

# 5. ENVIRONMENT ISOLATION

Do not force all research repositories into one Python environment.

Prefer:

    env-core
    env-geochat
    env-changechat
    env-croma

Expose each model through a stable internal interface/API. The core
application must communicate through capability contracts, not
through repository-specific implementation details.

## 5.1 PLATFORM RECOMMENDATION *(v4 addition)*

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Windows is not the recommended primary development environment**
> for this project. PyTorch + CUDA + GDAL + Rasterio + Flash Attention
> + research repositories have extensive known issues on Windows.

Recommended setup:

```
Windows host
    ↓
WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04+)
    ↓
NVIDIA CUDA toolkit (WSL2 driver)
    ↓
conda-forge (for GDAL/Rasterio binary deps)
    ↓
Docker (optional, for GeoChat service isolation)
```

The GUI/frontend runs in the browser on the Windows host.
Backend, ML, and GIS services run inside WSL2.

Do not make WSL2 mandatory if the native environment proves stable,
but make it the recommended reproducible path. All CI/deployment
should target Linux.

Avoid importing both raw `gdal` Python bindings and `rasterio` in
the same environment — they conflict at the C-library level.

---

# 6. RUNTIME MODES

Implement:

    runtime.mode = auto

Supported runtime states:

    FULL_AI
    HYBRID          ← the expected default state — see §8.2
    DEMO_FALLBACK

At startup: system check → model preflight (incl. license gate) →
capability registry → runtime mode. The UI must visibly show the
current mode at all times, e.g.:

    ● HYBRID MODE
      GeoChat available (optical VQA)
      SAR VQA: deterministic SAR feature tools
      ChangeChat unavailable (BLOCKED_LICENSE)
      Deterministic change engine active

Never silently substitute a generic model and pretend it is the
intended RS-VLM.

---

# 7. CAPABILITY REGISTRY

Models are represented as capabilities, selected by the router, not
hardcoded per task. Use machine-safe, lowercase, ASCII-only
capability and model IDs everywhere (see §40).

**Updated registry (v4):**

```yaml
single_image_vqa:
  optical:
    - geochat
    - approved_rs_vlm_fallback
    - demo_fallback
  sar:                                    # v4 addition
    - sar_adapted_vlm                     # SAR-capable pathway
    - sar_deterministic_feature_tools     # deterministic SAR analysis
    - demo_fallback

single_image_grounding:
  - geochat
  - deterministic_grounding_fallback      # v4: explicit fallback definition
  - demo_fallback

single_image_caption:
  - geochat
  - demo_fallback

temporal_change:
  - deterministic_change_engine           # always required — §16
  - changechat                            # optional explanation layer
  - demo_fallback

optical_sar_analysis:
  - optical_sar_fusion_engine             # always required — §17
  - croma_enhanced_analyzer               # optional
```

Every capability entry must declare: name, task, supported
modalities, **sensor compatibility**, required inputs, optional
inputs, outputs, dependencies, availability, device, status,
fallback capability.

**Grounding fallback rule (v4 addition):**

If GeoChat is unavailable, the grounding fallback must be one of:

1. A deterministic pipeline: query → object/category extraction →
   detector/segmentation → candidate regions → text-region matching
   → bbox. This is acceptable.
2. Explicitly declared: `GROUNDING: UNAVAILABLE`. This is acceptable.

A generic CV detector that does not perform text-guided region
selection must NOT be labeled "text-guided grounding." This follows
the Golden Rule.

---

# 8. FINAL MODEL REGISTRY

## 8.1 GeoChat

Primary specialist for **optical/multispectral** single-image VQA,
RS image understanding, grounding, region-level understanding,
captioning where supported.

Do not replace it with a generic LLaVA/CLIP/chat model merely
because integration is easier. If unavailable, activate the
registered fallback — never claim the fallback is equivalent.

**License chain:** GeoChat (Apache-2.0) → LLaVA-1.5 → Vicuna-v1.5 →
Llama 2 (Meta Community License). Must be fully documented in
`docs/model_licenses.md`.

## 8.2 ChangeChat — OPTIONAL, HYBRID mode is the EXPECTED default

ChangeChat requires approximately 48GB-class NVIDIA GPU memory.
This rules out essentially all single consumer GPUs. Treat it as
the exception, not the norm.

ChangeChat integration should only proceed if, in this exact order:

1. the License Gate (§4.1) passes;
2. the checkpoint can legally be used;
3. the team has access to suitable GPU compute (Profile A);
4. the model passes the actual preflight inference test.

If any step fails: mark ChangeChat unavailable and continue.
Deterministic Change Engine = the production temporal engine, full
stop. ChangeChat, when available, is only an optional
language/explanation enhancement layered on top of it.

**The SIH demo must be fully convincing without ChangeChat.** Do not
design the presentation or the team's expectations around it being
available.

Give ChangeChat a hard integration/debugging budget of 3 hours,
starting only after the License Gate passes. If unsuccessful after
that budget, mark unavailable and move on.

## 8.3 Deterministic Change Engine — MANDATORY, ALWAYS REQUIRED

Must work completely independently of ChangeChat.

```
T1 + T2 → metadata validation → spatial registration →
registration quality gate (§16.2) → common grid →
change computation → thresholding → mask cleanup →
connected components → geometry → measurement
```

Output structured evidence, e.g.:

```json
{
  "change_detected": true,
  "change_level": "physical",
  "regions": [{"id": "change_001", "bbox": [...], "area": 1.74}],
  "changed_area": 2.81,
  "unit": "hectares",
  "mask_path": "...",
  "semantic_class": null,
  "registration_quality": {"status": "PASS", "residual_px": 0.73}
}
```

No LLM-generated numerical value may override this result.

## 8.4 Optical-SAR Fusion Engine — MANDATORY

Do NOT make CROMA a requirement for this capability.

```
Optical → optical feature extraction → optical evidence
SAR     → SAR feature extraction     → SAR evidence
optical evidence + SAR evidence → spatial fusion →
fused result → confidence
```

Optical evidence candidates: RGB/false color, NDVI, NDWI, NDBI,
spectral ratios — only use an index if the necessary bands exist;
never assume all optical imagery has the same bands.

SAR evidence candidates: backscatter, polarization, texture,
relative intensity, spatial patterns. Do NOT use universal
hard-coded SAR thresholds — thresholds must be configurable,
documented, and validated on development data, never claimed to be
physically universal.

## 8.5 CROMA — OPTIONAL, stretch only

CROMA produces multimodal representations. It does NOT automatically
constitute a water/built-up/change detector. If used for a
downstream task, implement and document the actual task-specific
head. Never write "CROMA detected water" unless an implemented task
head actually produced that result. If CROMA integration causes
dependency or compute problems, disable it without affecting
mandatory functionality.

## 8.6 SENSOR-SPECIFIC VQA *(v4 addition — addresses SAR VQA gap)*

> [!CAUTION]
> Single-image VQA must be **sensor-aware**. The PS explicitly
> includes single SAR images in the supported input scope.
>
> A generic RGB-oriented RS-VLM must NOT be declared a valid SAR-VQA
> implementation merely because a SAR image can technically be
> converted into an RGB PNG. That is a critical scientific distinction.

The VQA router must branch on detected sensor modality:

```
single_image_vqa
│
├── optical / multispectral
│   ↓
│   geochat (or approved RS-VLM)
│
└── SAR
    ↓
    sar_vqa_capability
    │
    ┌───────┴────────┐
    │                │
    SAR-adapted    deterministic
    VLM            SAR feature
    (if available)  tools
```

**SAR VQA deterministic tools** must include at minimum:
- Backscatter statistics (mean, std, histogram)
- Polarization analysis (VV/VH ratio where available)
- Texture features (GLCM or equivalent)
- Basic classification (water/non-water via validated thresholds)
- Scene-level metadata description

The system must declare which VQA pathway was used in the execution

## 8.7 SAR INPUT ADAPTER *(v4 addition)*

When a SAR raster is supplied to a VLM whose vision encoder expects
RGB input (e.g., GeoChat's CLIP ViT-L/14 336px tower), an explicit
**sensor adapter** must be used:

```
SAR Input Adapter
│
├── SAR VV channel
├── SAR VH channel
├── VV/VH ratio or log-scaled backscatter
│
↓
SAR → 3-channel pseudo-RGB representation
↓
VLM inference
```

**Rules:**
1. This does NOT make the model "SAR-native." Document it as
   "SAR input adapter for VLM inference."
2. Evaluate SAR VQA results **separately** from optical VQA results.
3. If SAR-specific performance is poor, the system must honestly
   report that limitation rather than presenting the result with
   the same confidence as optical VQA.

# 16. TEMPORAL CHANGE PIPELINE — DETERMINISTIC-FIRST ARCHITECTURE

This is the corrected, final flow. The deterministic engine is not a
fallback bolted onto ChangeChat — it is the primary path:

```
                 BI-TEMPORAL QUERY
                        │
                        ▼
              Compatibility / Registration
                        │
                        ▼
              Registration Quality Gate (§16.2)
                        │
                        ▼
              Temporal Confound Check (§16.3)
                        │
                        ▼
               Deterministic Change Engine
                        │
              ┌─────────┴─────────┐
              ▼                   ▼
       L1: Physical         Geometry / Area
       Change Mask          Measurement
              │                   │
              └─────────┬─────────┘
                         ▼
              L2: Semantic Change (if classifier available)
                         │
                         ▼
                  Evidence Store
                         │
              ┌──────────┴──────────┐
              │                     │
        ChangeChat available   ChangeChat NOT
        (License Gate passed,   available
         Profile A GPU,              │
         preflight PASS)             │
              │                      │
              ▼                      ▼
      ChangeChat explanation   Template/rule-based
      layered on top of the    explanation generated
      verified mask/measurement   from the verified
                                    mask/measurement
              │                      │
              └──────────┬───────────┘
                          ▼
                   Verified Answer
```

ChangeChat explains evidence; it must never invent it.

## 16.1 SEMANTIC-CHANGE BOUNDARY *(v4 addition)*

> [!CAUTION]
> A change mask does NOT constitute semantic change classification.
> Binary/image change ≠ semantic change.

The system must distinguish two levels:

```
LEVEL 1 — Physical / image change
    pixel, spectral, or backscatter difference
    Output: change_detected, change_region, change_measurement

LEVEL 2 — Semantic change
    building, road, vegetation, water, bare soil, etc.
    Output: change_type_inferred, semantic_class, semantic_confidence
```

**Rules:**
- `change_detected` = Level 1 (always available from deterministic engine)
- `change_type_inferred` = Level 2 (only if a semantic classifier
  actually supports the claim)
- No semantic class may be asserted solely from a binary difference mask
- The response must declare which level was achieved:

```json
{
  "change_detected": true,
  "change_level": "physical",
  "change_type_inferred": null,
  "note": "Semantic change classification not available — only physical change detected"
}
```

vs:

```json
{
  "change_detected": true,
  "change_level": "semantic",
  "change_type_inferred": "vegetation_loss",
  "semantic_confidence": 0.78,
  "semantic_source": "land_cover_classifier_v1"
}
```

## 16.2 REGISTRATION QUALITY GATE *(v4 addition)*

Registration can fail silently. A 4-pixel shift between T1 and T2
will produce false "change" across the entire image.

The registration step must produce a quality assessment:

```json
{
  "registration_status": "PASS",
  "method": "arosics_local_coreg",
  "residual_px": 0.73,
  "overlap_fraction": 0.94,
  "source_crs": "EPSG:32643",
  "target_crs": "EPSG:32643",
  "resampling": "bilinear"
}
```

**Status values:** `PASS` / `WARN` / `REJECT`

**Rules:**
- Do NOT hardcode the residual threshold — it must be configurable
  and validated on development data.
- If registration quality is `REJECT`, temporal analysis must STOP.
- If registration quality is `WARN`, temporal analysis may proceed
  but the result must be explicitly marked:
  `"reliability": "reduced — registration residual elevated"`
- This is especially important for the hidden Cartosat-2S/RISAT
  evaluation data, which may have different alignment
  characteristics than Sentinel development data.

**Recommended tool:** AROSICS (`pip install arosics`) for automated
sub-pixel co-registration with tie-point detection.

## 16.3 TEMPORAL CONFOUND WARNING *(v4 addition)*

Temporal change detection is vulnerable to false positives from
non-change sources. The system must check for and report potential
confounders:

| Confound | Check |
|:--|:--|
| Illumination differences | Sun elevation/azimuth from metadata |
| Seasonal differences | Acquisition month comparison |
| Crop cycles | Season + known agricultural context |
| Atmospheric effects | Processing level (L1C vs L2A) |
| Sensor/viewing geometry | Incidence angle for SAR |
| SAR speckle | Speckle statistics |
| Preprocessing differences | Product type comparison |
| Resolution mismatch | GSD comparison |
| Shadow artifacts | Sun angle + terrain if available |
| Cloud/nodata | Nodata mask, cloud mask for optical |

When potential confounders are detected, the evidence must include:

```json
{
  "temporal_confounds": [
    {"type": "seasonal", "detail": "T1=June, T2=December", "risk": "high"},
    {"type": "resolution", "detail": "T1=10m, T2=0.65m", "risk": "medium"}
  ],
  "confound_warning": "Change detected, but seasonal/resolution differences may contribute to observed difference."
}
```

# 17. OPTICAL-SAR ANALYSIS

Build OpticalSARAnalyzer: validate metadata → validate spatial
compatibility → co-register → create common grid → extract optical
evidence → extract SAR evidence → perform spatial fusion →
calculate evidence-level confidence → produce structured result →
generate explanation. Confidence must not be presented as a
calibrated probability unless calibration has actually been
performed.

## 17.1 CONCRETE OPTICAL-SAR FUSION ALGORITHM *(v4 addition)*

> [!IMPORTANT]
> An evaluator can ask: "What exactly is your fusion algorithm?"
> The answer must be concrete, not conceptual.
>
> "Fusion" cannot mean merely displaying two independent results
> side by side. The contribution of each modality must be
> identifiable in the evidence object and ablation/test output.

Every mandatory optical-SAR demonstration must use an **explicitly
implemented, task-specific fusion rule or model.**

**Required baseline — water body detection:**

```
OPTICAL BRANCH:
  available bands
      ↓
  NDWI / MNDWI (if Green + SWIR available)
  or NDVI < threshold (if NIR + Red available)
      ↓
  optical water candidate mask + confidence

SAR BRANCH:
  VV / VH (or available polarization)
      ↓
  calibrated / normalized backscatter
      ↓
  development-validated water threshold
  (low VV + low VH → water candidate)
      ↓
  SAR water candidate mask + confidence

FUSION:
  optical water evidence + SAR water evidence
      ↓
  spatial alignment to common grid
      ↓
  agreement map:
    BOTH agree water    → HIGH confidence
    optical only        → MODERATE (may be shadow/cloud)
    SAR only           → MODERATE (may be smooth surface)
    neither            → NOT water
      ↓
  fused water mask + per-pixel confidence source
```

**Rules:**
- Weights/thresholds must be derived from development data, not
  hardcoded universal values.
- The evidence object must identify which modality contributed:

```json
{
  "claim": "Water body detected",
  "optical_evidence": "NDWI > 0.3 (strong)",
  "sar_evidence": "VV backscatter < -15 dB (moderate)",
  "fusion_agreement": "both_agree",
  "confidence": "high",
  "confidence_basis": "spatial_agreement"
}
```

- If only one modality is available (partial pair), the system
  must still function but declare reduced confidence.

# 19. NUMERICAL GUARD

The language model must NEVER invent measurements. The measurement
engine computes the number; the response generator receives it; the
LLM may only verbalize a value it was given. Same rule for area,
pixel count, coordinates, distances, dates, resolutions, confidence
values, counts.

# 20. VERIFICATION ENGINE

Implement EvidenceVerifier, checking numerical consistency, region
consistency, mask existence, bbox validity, input provenance,
temporal consistency, output provenance, model/tool availability. If
verification fails, mark the result as uncertain rather than
silently producing a confident answer.

**Concrete verification rules (v4):**
- `area_km2 == pixel_count × (resolution_m)² / 1e6` (within 1% tolerance)
- `bbox` coordinates must fall within input image bounds
- `confidence` values must be in [0.0, 1.0]
- Temporal dates must satisfy `T1 < T2`
- Model-generated text must not contain numbers not present in the
  evidence store

**Mid-pipeline crash recovery (v4):** Every pipeline stage must have
`try/except → fallback → log`. A model that loads but crashes during
inference on a specific image must not crash the entire pipeline.

## 25.1 CONFIDENCE TYPE DECOMPOSITION *(v4 addition)*

Do not present a single `overall_confidence = 0.84` unless it is
actually calibrated.

Instead, decompose:

```json
{
  "confidence": {
    "model_confidence": 0.84,
    "evidence_confidence": "high",
    "measurement_quality": "computed",
    "registration_quality": "PASS (0.73px)",
    "fusion_agreement": "both_agree",
    "analysis_source": "deterministic"
  }
}
```

**Rules:**
- `model_confidence`: raw model output probability (if available)
- `evidence_confidence`: qualitative assessment (`high`/`moderate`/`low`)
  based on evidence agreement and completeness
- `measurement_quality`: `computed` / `estimated` / `heuristic`
- `registration_quality`: from §16.2 gate
- `fusion_agreement`: from §17.1 fusion algorithm

If a validated, calibrated score exists, present it as:

```
Calibrated confidence: 0.91
Calibration method: isotonic regression
Validation set: BigEarthNet-v2 dev split (N=500)
```

Otherwise, do NOT use percentage format — use qualitative labels.

# 28. MANDATORY DEMONSTRATION SCENARIOS

**DEMO 1 — Single-image optical VQA:** upload optical image, ask a
land-cover question → RS-VLM answer + evidence + confidence + trace.

**DEMO 2 — Grounding:** "Where is the largest water body?" → bbox/region
+ overlay + answer + confidence.

**DEMO 3 — Bi-temporal change:** T1+T2, "What changed?" → before/after +
change mask + measurements + L1/L2 distinction + explanation
(ChangeChat if available, fallback otherwise).

**DEMO 4 — Optical-SAR fusion:** optical+SAR, "Identify regions likely
to contain surface water using both observations" → optical evidence +
SAR evidence + **fusion agreement map** + **per-modality contribution** +

**DEMO 5 — Agentic routing:** different queries against the same data
automatically select VQA / grounding / change / optical-SAR without
manual model selection.

**DEMO 6 — Failure handling:** one image only, "What changed?" → precise
refusal, no hallucinated second observation.

**DEMO 7 — Compute fallback:** with GeoChat or ChangeChat disabled, show
the HYBRID/DEMO_FALLBACK indicator, the unavailable capability, the
active fallback, and continued operation.

ask a question → SAR-specific analysis + sensor adapter declaration +
honest capability boundary.

# 29. PRIORITY SYSTEM *(Updated v4 — resolves P0/P1 contradiction)*

**P0 — MUST WORK (capability level):**

Upload, GeoTIFF validation, metadata extraction, query
classification, sensor-aware router, single-image VQA **workflow**
(optical + SAR pathways), grounding **workflow**, change detection
(with registration quality gate + L1/L2 distinction), optical-SAR
fusion (with concrete algorithm), evidence store, execution trace,
GUI (with truthfulness layer), reports, failure handling.

**P1 — HIGH VALUE (implementation quality):**

GeoChat **live inference**, ChangeChat live inference, BigEarthNet.txt
LoRA adaptation reaching `RS_ADAPTATION_TRAINED` or
`RS_ADAPTATION_EVALUATED`, semantic change classification (L2),
SAR-adapted VLM.

**P0 defines the workflow contract. P1 defines the best implementation
of that contract.** The system must function at P0 even when all P1
components are unavailable.

A valid P0 build requires at least one working RS-adapted VL
component (the PS requirement). If no large VLM is available,
a smaller adapted model (e.g., fine-tuned classifier + deterministic
tools) can satisfy P0, but a completely generic fallback cannot.

**P2 — ENHANCEMENT:**

CROMA, richer change semantics, advanced calibration, offline field
pack, additional sensor support.

Never sacrifice P0 to implement P2.

---

# 30. DO NOT BUILD

Do not spend hackathon time on: training a giant VLM from scratch,
building a new LLM, building a CROMA task head before core
functionality works, universal satellite support, every possible SAR
polarization, real-time satellite streaming, NavIC integration,
VHF/offline communications, mobile app, Kubernetes, distributed
inference infrastructure, elaborate cloud architecture, adding more
models to solve architectural risks — unless all P0/P1 requirements
are already stable.

> The temptation to add EarthGPT + Grounding DINO + SAM + CLIP +
> another SAR model + another change model will make the project
> worse. The current architecture's strongest idea is: **specialist
> models are replaceable components; the evidence-driven SatQuery
> workflow is the product.**

---

# 31. SCIENTIFIC INTEGRITY RULES

Never fabricate accuracy, IoU, confidence, area, coordinates,
benchmark results, training results, dataset counts, model
capabilities, or sensor specifications. If something was not
measured, say "not measured." If a model did not run, say
"unavailable." If a result is heuristic, label it "heuristic." If a
result is computed, identify the computational source. If a model is
a fallback, label it as fallback. If a change is physical (L1), do
not claim it is semantic (L2).

---

# 32. NO FAKE PRECISION

Do not hard-code impressive-looking numbers (e.g. "18.40 km²,"
"92.4% accuracy," "0.91 confidence," "0.95 IoU") unless those values
came from an actual executed experiment on actual input data.

Confidence display rules:
- If calibrated: show as decimal with calibration method
- If not calibrated: show as qualitative (`HIGH` / `MODERATE` / `LOW`)
- Never display `91%` — it implies calibrated probability

---

# 33. DATA / SENSOR ASSUMPTIONS

Never assume a specific number of optical bands, a particular SAR
polarization, a universal spatial resolution, universal SAR
backscatter thresholds, universal cloud behavior, or universal
sensor calibration constants. Use product metadata; report the
limitation if a required property is missing. SAR calibration must
be metadata/product-aware — never a universal DN → sigma0 formula.

---

# 34. CODE QUALITY

Typed Python where practical, Pydantic schemas, structured logging,
configuration files, environment variables, unit tests, integration
tests, reproducible scripts, README, setup instructions, model setup
documentation. Avoid one giant file — separate gateway, contracts,
router, tools, models, evidence, verification, reporting, API,
frontend.

---

# 35. LOGGING

Every execution produces structured logs: `execution_id`, `timestamp`,
`input_ids`, `query`, `detected_task`, `detected_sensor`,
`selected_capability`, `selected_model`, `fallback_used`,
`analysis_source`, `parameters`, `duration`, `outputs`,
`verification_status`, `registration_quality`, `temporal_confounds`.

**DO NOT BUILD A COLLECTION OF AI MODELS. BUILD SATQUERY AI.**

optional specialist. The SatQuery controller, evidence layer,
verification layer, data-readiness gate, fallback architecture,
sensor-aware routing, and multimodal workflow are the actual system.

Do not begin the next day's work on an uncommitted or unverified
state. If a later day's work breaks the system, restore the most
recent stable checkpoint.

# 42. ANTIGRAVITY EXECUTION PROTOCOL (READ BEFORE STARTING)

This document is the master specification: architecture,
requirements, priorities, constraints, and acceptance criteria.

**Do not execute all eight days continuously in one unattended run.**
Work in one-day milestones, human-reviewed between each.

At the beginning of each day's session:

1. Inspect the current repository.
2. Read the previous day's `docs/dayN_report.md`.
3. Verify the previous stable Git tag exists and is checked out.
4. Check the current capability registry state.
5. Determine what is ACTUALLY implemented rather than assuming
   planned features exist.
6. Execute only the current day's scope (§27).

At the end of each day's session:

1. Run tests.
2. Start the application and verify it runs.
3. Verify the day's acceptance criteria.
4. Update `docs/dayN_report.md`.
5. Record blockers and fallback paths used.
6. Commit.
7. Create the day's stable Git tag.

```
"Execute Day 2 only."
        │
        ▼
[review] → "Execute Day 3 only." → [review] → ... → Day 8
```

Never issue "build everything, Days 1 through 8" as a single
instruction.

    4. As of this specification, no clear LICENSE file could be
       confirmed for ChangeChat's repository — treat as
       BLOCKED_LICENSE by default until the team independently
       verifies otherwise. Do not proceed to inference preflight
       until this is resolved.
    5. The deterministic temporal change pipeline (Section 16)
       remains the official implementation regardless of this gate's
       outcome.

Run the same independent license verification for CROMA before
relying on its weights. Record all three (GeoChat, ChangeChat,
CROMA) in docs/model_licenses.md, regardless of outcome.

============================================================
5. ENVIRONMENT ISOLATION
============================================================

Do not force all research repositories into one Python environment.
Prefer `env-core`, `env-geochat`, `env-changechat`, `env-croma`.
Expose each model through a stable internal interface/API — the core
application communicates through capability contracts, never
repository-specific implementation details.

============================================================
6. RUNTIME MODES
============================================================

    runtime.mode = auto
    states: FULL_AI | HYBRID | DEMO_FALLBACK

At startup: system check → model preflight (incl. license gates) →
capability registry → runtime mode. The UI must always visibly show
current mode and exactly which capability is running on which
mechanism, e.g.:

    ● HYBRID MODE
      Core GIS / Change / Fusion / Evidence / Reports   READY (local)
      GeoChat                                            REMOTE
      SAR VQA (deterministic pathway)                     READY (local)
      ChangeChat                                          BLOCKED_LICENSE
      CROMA                                                DISABLED

Never silently substitute a generic model and pretend it is the
intended RS-VLM. Never silently substitute a deterministic pathway's
output and call it a model's output, or vice versa.

============================================================
7. CAPABILITY REGISTRY
============================================================

Models are capabilities, selected by the router, never hardcoded per
task. Use machine-safe, lowercase, ASCII-only IDs everywhere (see
Section 41 — no visually confusable Unicode characters in any
identifier, e.g. never a Cyrillic "О" where Latin "O" is meant).

    single_image_vqa_optical
      ├── geochat
      ├── approved_rs_vlm_fallback
      └── demo_fallback

    single_image_vqa_sar
      ├── sar_adapted_vlm            (only if one is actually verified)
      ├── sar_input_adapter_to_vlm   (labeled honestly — Section 9)
      └── sar_deterministic_features (always available — Section 8)

    single_image_grounding
      ├── geochat
      └── demo_fallback

    temporal_change
      ├── deterministic_change_engine   (always required — Section 16)
      ├── changechat                    (optional explanation layer)
      └── demo_fallback

    optical_sar_analysis
      ├── optical_sar_fusion_engine     (always required — Section 18)
      └── croma_enhanced_analyzer       (optional)

Every capability entry declares: name, task, supported modalities,
required/optional inputs, outputs, dependencies, availability,
device, status, fallback capability.

============================================================
8. FINAL MODEL REGISTRY
============================================================

8.1 GeoChat — primary optical specialist (VQA, region understanding,
grounding, captioning where supported). See Section 4.1 for its
license chain. Never replace with a generic LLaVA/CLIP/chat model
for ease of integration. If unavailable, activate the registered
fallback and never claim equivalence.

8.2 ChangeChat — OPTIONAL. Requires ~48GB-class VRAM per its own
published hardware requirements — this rules out essentially all
single consumer GPUs. **HYBRID mode (deterministic engine, no
ChangeChat) is the expected default outcome, not an edge case.**
Integration proceeds only if, in order: (1) License Gate passes,
(2) checkpoint legally usable, (3) Profile A compute available,
(4) preflight passes. Hard integration budget: 3 hours, starting
only after the license gate passes. If unsuccessful, mark
unavailable and continue — the SIH demo must be fully convincing
without it.

8.3 Deterministic Change Engine — MANDATORY, always required,
works fully independently of ChangeChat. See Section 16.

8.4 Optical-SAR Fusion Engine — MANDATORY, no CROMA dependency.
See Section 18.

8.5 SAR Deterministic Feature Tools — MANDATORY (new in v4). See
Section 8/9/10. Provides VV/VH statistics, VV/VH ratio, histogram,
texture/GLCM, spatial intensity patterns, and validated water/
non-water analysis directly from calibrated backscatter — the always
available baseline for SAR-image questions, independent of any VLM.

8.6 CROMA — OPTIONAL, stretch only. Produces representations, not
answers — never write "CROMA detected water" unless an actual
trained task head produced that result.

============================================================
9. SENSOR-AWARE ROUTING — SAR GETS ITS OWN PATHWAY
============================================================

The system must NOT treat:

    SAR → pseudo-RGB conversion → GeoChat → "SAR VQA"

as genuine SAR understanding. GeoChat is trained on optical imagery;
it has no grounded basis for interpreting radar backscatter
semantics from a color-mapped SAR image.

    QUERY
      │
      ▼
    Sensor Detection
      │
      ├── OPTICAL  → GeoChat (Section 13)
      ├── SAR      → SAR pathway (this section)
      └── MULTIMODAL → Pair Analyzer (Section 18)

SAR pathway, in priority order:

    1. If a genuinely SAR-adapted VLM is available and verified
       (not just "a VLM that accepted a SAR-derived image"):
       SAR Input Adapter → SAR-adapted VLM → VQA.
    2. Otherwise (the expected default): SAR deterministic feature
       tools (Section 8.5) → structured answer, composed by the
       response generator from real computed statistics, never from
       an LLM guessing at a radar image.

If a generic RGB-oriented VLM is used with a converted pseudo-RGB
SAR input, the execution trace and UI MUST label the pathway exactly
as:

    SAR pathway: SAR input adapter → VLM (not SAR-native)

never as "SAR-native VLM" or unqualified "SAR VQA," unless the model
was actually trained/adapted specifically for SAR.

============================================================
10. SAR INPUT ADAPTER (for the optional VLM path)
============================================================

    VV, VH, VV/VH → normalization → 3-channel pseudo-RGB → VLM

The report and execution trace must always declare this conversion
happened. This is a legitimate technique to get *some* VLM signal
from SAR data, but it is never equivalent to a model trained natively
on radar backscatter — label it as such every time it's used.

============================================================
11. GROUNDING
============================================================

Primary: GeoChat. Output: object, bbox, confidence, evidence image,
analysis_source. If GeoChat is unavailable, only two legitimate
outcomes exist: a genuinely valid text-guided grounding fallback, or
"GROUNDING: UNAVAILABLE." A generic object detector must never be
mislabeled as text-guided grounding.

============================================================
12. INPUT GATEWAY
============================================================

Support GeoTIFF, TIFF, PNG/JPEG only where permitted by the relevant
benchmark/demo. For each raster extract dimensions, CRS, transform,
bounds, resolution, band count/metadata, nodata, acquisition time,
modality, sensor metadata where available. Reject corrupted files,
unsupported formats, missing required inputs, incompatible pairs,
insufficient bands for the requested operation, missing timestamps
for temporal analysis.

============================================================
13. DATA READINESS GATE
============================================================

Build RasterInspector, CompatibilityChecker, TemporalChecker,
CoRegistrationChecker. For pairs check CRS, bounds, spatial overlap,
dimensions, resolution, affine transform, acquisition timestamp,
nodata, modality, band availability. If reprojection/resampling is
required, perform it explicitly and record source CRS, target CRS,
resampling method, output resolution. Never silently modify input
data.

============================================================
14. QUERY CONTRACT
============================================================

Convert natural language into structured intent, e.g.:

    {
      "intent": "temporal_change",
      "requires_temporal_pair": true,
      "requires_spatial_evidence": true,
      "requested_outputs": ["description", "change_region"],
      "measurement_required": false
    }

Supported task types: single_image_vqa_optical,
single_image_vqa_sar, single_image_grounding, single_image_caption,
temporal_change, optical_sar_analysis, unsupported.

============================================================
15. AGENTIC ROUTER
============================================================

Determines: task requested, inputs available, capability that
satisfies the task, availability on this machine, fallback,
required tool sequence. If a required input is missing, refuse with
a technical explanation:

    Cannot perform temporal change analysis.
    Reason: Only one acquisition was supplied.
    Required: Two temporally distinct observations.

Never hallucinate missing observations.

============================================================
16. TEMPORAL CHANGE PIPELINE — REGISTRATION-GATED, L1/L2-AWARE
============================================================

Deterministic-first, ChangeChat-optional flow:

                 BI-TEMPORAL QUERY
                        │
                        ▼
              Compatibility / Registration
                        │
                        ▼
             Registration Quality Gate
              (see 16.1 — AROSICS-based)
                        │
              PASS ─────┼───── WARN ─────┼───── REJECT
                        │                │        │
                        ▼                ▼        ▼
              Temporal Confound      continue    STOP —
              Check (16.2)           w/ reduced  report
                        │             reliability misalignment,
                        ▼             warning     no change
              Deterministic Change                claimed
              Engine
                        │
              ┌─────────┴─────────┐
              ▼                   ▼
        Change Mask (L1)     Geometry / Area
              │                   │
              └─────────┬─────────┘
                         ▼
                  L1/L2 Declaration (16.3)
                         │
                  Evidence Store
                         │
              ┌──────────┴──────────┐
        ChangeChat available   ChangeChat NOT
        (license+GPU+preflight    available
         all passed)                  │
              │                       │
              ▼                       ▼
      Explanation layered on   Template/rule-based
      the verified mask/       explanation from the
      measurement               verified mask/measurement
              │                       │
              └──────────┬────────────┘
                          ▼
                   Verified Answer

------------------------------------------------------------
16.1 Registration Quality Gate
------------------------------------------------------------

Use AROSICS (real, open-source, Apache-2.0, GFZ Potsdam — Scheffler
et al. 2017, subpixel frequency-domain co-registration with built-in
outlier/cloud detection) or an equivalent verified method. Compute
residual/RMSE and overlap; classify PASS / WARN / REJECT.

    REJECT → STOP temporal analysis. Report the misalignment reason.
             Do not run change detection on misregistered imagery.
    WARN   → continue, but attach a reduced-reliability warning to
             every downstream claim.
    PASS   → proceed normally.

This prevents simple spatial misalignment from being interpreted as
physical change.

------------------------------------------------------------
16.2 Temporal Confound Check
------------------------------------------------------------

Check for and report: illumination difference, season, crop cycle,
atmospheric conditions, sensor geometry difference, SAR speckle,
resolution mismatch, cloud cover, nodata, processing-level
difference. Output a temporal reliability state: HIGH / MODERATE /
LOW. `T1 ≠ T2` does not automatically mean real-world change — this
check is what stands between a pixel difference and a defensible
claim.

------------------------------------------------------------
16.3 L1 vs L2 — mandatory declaration on every change answer
------------------------------------------------------------

L1 — PHYSICAL/IMAGE CHANGE (always available): pixel difference,
spectral difference, backscatter difference → change_detected,
change_region, change_mask, changed_area.

L2 — SEMANTIC CHANGE (only when an actual classifier supports it):
"building constructed," "vegetation removed," "water expanded,"
"road created." Never derive an L2 label from a binary mask alone.

If no semantic classifier is implemented, every change response
must explicitly say:

    Change detected.
    Level: PHYSICAL CHANGE
    Semantic interpretation: NOT AVAILABLE

============================================================
17. GEOCHAT / OPTICAL VQA IMPLEMENTATION
============================================================

Image + question → answer, confidence where available, model name,
evidence, provenance. Then grounding (bbox/region + overlay +
confidence + description). Captioning when supported.

============================================================
18. OPTICAL-SAR FUSION — CONCRETE ALGORITHM, NOT SIDE-BY-SIDE
============================================================

Must be a real fusion algorithm, not two results merely displayed
next to each other.

    OPTICAL → NDWI/MNDWI (only if the required bands exist) →
      optical water/feature mask
    SAR → VV/VH backscatter analysis (Section 8.5) →
      SAR water/feature mask
    Both masks → COMMON GRID (post-registration) → Spatial Agreement

Fusion confidence tiers, explicit and structured (not a single fake
percentage):

    BOTH AGREE     → HIGH
    OPTICAL ONLY   → MODERATE (cloud-free but SAR disagrees/missing)
    SAR ONLY       → MODERATE (cloud-obscured optical, SAR-only
                      evidence — this is exactly the "SAR sees
                      through clouds" case the PS cares about)
    NEITHER        → NOT PRESENT

Output structured result:

    {
      "class": "water",
      "optical_evidence": {...},
      "sar_evidence": {...},
      "fusion": {"agreement": "both_agree", "tier": "HIGH"},
      "regions": [...]
    }

Never use universal hard-coded SAR thresholds — thresholds must be
configurable, documented, and validated on development data.
The contribution of each modality must always be independently
identifiable in the output (never collapse to a single number with
no per-modality breakdown).

============================================================
19. EVIDENCE STORE
============================================================

    {
      "claim": "A water body is present",
      "source": "optical_sar_fusion",
      "evidence_type": "region",
      "bbox": [...],
      "confidence": {"evidence": "high", "fusion_agreement": "both_agree"},
      "inputs": ["sentinel2_01", "sentinel1_01"],
      "analysis_source": "deterministic"
    }

Evidence types: region, bbox, mask, measurement, metadata,
model_output, temporal_difference.

============================================================
20. CONFIDENCE ARCHITECTURE — DECOMPOSED, NEVER A FAKE SINGLE NUMBER
============================================================

Never present:

    Confidence = 91%

as if it were one calibrated probability. Instead:

    {
      "model_confidence": "...",
      "evidence_confidence": "HIGH",
      "measurement_quality": "COMPUTED",
      "registration_quality": "PASS",
      "fusion_agreement": "BOTH_AGREE",
      "analysis_source": "DETERMINISTIC"
    }

Treat these as system evidence states, not scientifically calibrated
probabilities, unless calibration has actually been performed and
measured.

============================================================
21. NUMERICAL GUARD
============================================================

The language model NEVER invents measurements — area, pixel count,
coordinates, distances, dates, resolutions, confidence values,
counts. The measurement engine computes the number; the response
generator receives it; the LLM may only verbalize a value it was
given, never a different one.

============================================================
22. VERIFICATION ENGINE
============================================================

EvidenceVerifier checks numerical consistency, region consistency,
mask existence, bbox validity, input provenance, temporal
consistency, output provenance, model/tool availability. If
verification fails, mark the result uncertain rather than silently
producing a confident answer.

============================================================
23. RS ADAPTATION — VERIFIABLE STATUS STATES (mandatory, high-risk)
============================================================

Do not conflate "we built an adaptation pipeline" with "we adapted a
model." Use explicit status states, and never claim a later state
than what actually executed:

    RS_ADAPTATION_PIPELINE_READY   ← manifest, subset, LoRA config exist
              ↓
    RS_ADAPTATION_TRAINED          ← a real training run executed and
                                       produced a checkpoint
              ↓
    RS_ADAPTATION_EVALUATED        ← baseline vs adapted results were
                                       actually measured and compared

Only TRAINED or EVALUATED count as completed adaptation evidence for
the PS's mandatory adaptation requirement. PIPELINE_READY alone does
not satisfy it — report it honestly as partial if that's as far as
the team got, and say so plainly in the final report rather than
implying more was done.

------------------------------------------------------------
23.1 Three-tier dataset strategy
------------------------------------------------------------

Do NOT download the entire BigEarthNet.txt corpus.

    Tier 1 — Metadata only: annotations, IDs, splits, task labels.
             Goal: a reproducible manifest.
    Tier 2 — Development subset: ~1,000–5,000 image pairs, sized to
             actual disk/bandwidth/GPU/time.
    Tier 3 — Task-filtered subset for the actual adaptation task
             (recommended first: image + question → answer). Example:
             1,000–3,000 train / 200–500 validation, adjusted to real
             resources. Record actual counts used — never fabricate.

------------------------------------------------------------
23.2 Execution strategy for constrained local hardware
------------------------------------------------------------

    LOCAL: metadata → subset generation → task filtering →
           train/validation manifest → training configuration
    REMOTE (free/cheap GPU burst): selected RS-VLM + subset →
           LoRA/PEFT → checkpoint → evaluation
    Bring back: adapter + evaluation results + configuration +
           checksums. Record base model, adapter config, dataset
           version, exact train/val counts, epochs/steps, learning
           rate, batch size, hardware, checkpoint, results. Report
           BASELINE and ADAPTED separately — never claim improvement
           unless measured. If training cannot complete, report that
           honestly and continue using the available RS-adapted
           model as-is (GeoChat's own pretraining already satisfies
           "at least one RS-adapted component" even if further
           LoRA adaptation stalls).

============================================================

============================================================

    EXECUTION TRACE
    ✓ Input validation
    ✓ GeoTIFF metadata extracted
    ✓ Sensor detected: SAR
    ✓ Query classified: SINGLE_IMAGE_VQA_SAR
    ✓ Pathway: SAR deterministic feature tools (not VLM)
    ✓ Measurements verified
    ✓ Evidence overlay generated
    ✓ Final response generated

Also show the selected tools list. Never expose hidden

32. 8-DAY IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (WITH DAILY CHECKPOINTS)
============================================================

Every day ends with the checkpoint ritual in Section 42.

DAY 1 — Core infrastructure + compute gate + test imagery. Build
repo, FastAPI, frontend shell, upload, GeoTIFF parser, metadata,
readiness gate, system_check.py. Acquire a small public Sentinel-1/
Sentinel-2 test corpus (single optical, single SAR, bi-temporal
pair, co-registered optical-SAR pair) into data/samples/ with a
recorded manifest — for engineering validation only, never presented
as equivalent to the hidden ISRO/SAC set. Milestone: upload →
inspect → validate, no VLM dependency. Checkpoint: `day-1-stable`.

DAY 2 — Query contract, sensor detection, capability registry,
router, execution trace, runtime mode. Milestone: different queries
route to different capabilities, including the SAR-vs-optical split.
Checkpoint: `day-2-stable`.

DAY 3 — GeoChat license note + preflight → VQA + grounding if
successful, else fallback. SAR deterministic feature tools (Section
8.5) — always build this regardless of GeoChat's outcome, since it
has zero GPU dependency. Do not spend the whole day on GeoChat
loading. Checkpoint: `day-3-stable`.

DAY 4 — BigEarthNet.txt Tier 1–3 subset, LoRA/PEFT pipeline
(local prep, remote GPU burst for the actual training run),
evaluation, honest status reporting per Section 23's state machine.
Checkpoint: `day-4-stable`.

DAY 5 — Temporal pipeline: registration → Registration Quality Gate
(AROSICS) → Temporal Confound Check → deterministic change engine →
L1 declaration → L2 only if a real classifier exists. ChangeChat
attempted only if license gate passed and Profile A compute is
available, hard-capped at 3 hours; expect HYBRID as the default
outcome. Checkpoint: `day-5-stable`.

DAY 6 — Optical-SAR: co-registration, NDWI/MNDWI optical evidence,
SAR backscatter evidence, common grid, concrete fusion algorithm
with agreement tiers (Section 18), visualization. CROMA optional,
never blocking. Checkpoint: `day-6-stable`.

DAY 7 — Evidence store, verification, numerical guard, confidence
decomposition, visual overlays, execution trace, reports (PDF/JSON/
GeoJSON), GUI polish. Checkpoint: `day-7-stable`.

DAY 8 — Run all 8 mandatory demos (Section 33) and the full
acceptance suite (Section 40). Freeze architecture. Fix only bugs,
integration problems, UI problems, reproducibility problems. No new
foundation model on Day 8. Checkpoint: `day-8-final`.

============================================================

DEMO 1 — Optical VQA: image + land-cover question → GeoChat answer +

DEMO 2 — Grounding: "Where is the largest water body?" → bbox +

36. SCIENTIFIC AND ENGINEERING INTEGRITY RULES
============================================================

Never fabricate accuracy, IoU, confidence, area, coordinates,
benchmark results, training results, dataset counts, model
capabilities, or sensor specifications. If something was not
measured, say "not measured." If a model did not run, say
"unavailable." If a result is heuristic, label it "heuristic." If a
pathway used a fallback or adapter, label it exactly as such — never
a shortened or more impressive-sounding name. Do not hard-code
impressive numbers (e.g. "18.40 km²," "92.4% accuracy," "0.95 IoU")
unless they came from an actual executed run on actual input data.
Never assume a fixed band count, SAR polarization, resolution,
backscatter threshold, or calibration constant — use product
metadata and report the limitation when a required property is
missing.

where Latin "O" is meant). Normalize to plain ASCII everywhere:

============================================================

 1. Can upload supported GeoTIFF? 2. Can inspect metadata? 3. Can
reject incompatible input? 4. Can classify a query by sensor and
